row.title: Conjecture on spectra and positive semistability of forest chromatic operators
row.statement: Let $F$ be a forest on $n$ vertices, let $\pi$ be an ordering of its edges, and let $\alpha_{F,\pi}\in\mathbb{C}[S_n]$ be its chromatic operator. A chromatic operator is **positive semistable** when all its eigenvalues have nonnegative real part. **Forest chromatic-operator conjecture.** (a) The characteristic polynomial of $\alpha_{F,\pi}$ does not depend on the edge ordering $\pi$. (b) The number of forests on $n$ vertices whose chromatic operator is positive semistable is $f_{n-1}$, where $f_n$ is the $n$th Fibonacci number, with $f_1=f_2=1$. The paper reports that part (b) has been checked up to $10$ vertices, while the general assertions remain conjectural.
row.source_name: Brendan Pawlowski, “Chromatic symmetric functions via the group algebra of S_n”, arXiv:1802.05470 (2024).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.05470

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2018).

row.title: Symmetry, unimodality, and factorial sum for diagonal numerators of the blade array
row.statement:
Let $T^B_{n,k}$ be the array whose entries count blades of dimension $n-k$ in the canonical basis of graduated blades, with diagonal generating functions formed from the corresponding diagonal sequences. Let the numerator polynomial of each such generating function have coefficient vector $(b_1,\ldots,b_m)$, where a vector is symmetric when $b_i=b_{m-i}$ and unimodal when its entries weakly increase to a peak and then weakly decrease. **Diagonal numerator conjecture.** The coefficients of the polynomial numerators of the generating functions for the diagonals of the array $T^B_{n,k}$ are symmetric and unimodal, and sum to the sequence

$$
a(m)=\frac{(2m)!}{m!}.
$$

The conjecture was verified numerically in Mathematica through the 24th diagonal, but a general proof is not given.
row.source_name: Nick Early, “Honeycomb Tessellations and Graded Permutohedral Blades”, arXiv:1810.03246 (2025).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1810.03246

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of October 2018). “The conjecture has been verified numerically in Mathematica: through the 24th diagonal.”

row.title: The pure 5d Nekrasov partition-function relation at special parameters
row.statement:
Let $\mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{inst}}(i,i,i,iq^{\pm1/2},u;q^{-1},q|z^{1/2})$ denote the five-dimensional Nekrasov instanton partition function with the displayed special values of $v_i$, and let $\mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{inst}}(u;q^{-1},q^2|z)$ denote the pure five-dimensional Nekrasov instanton partition function with $\epsilon_2=-2\epsilon_1$. **Nekrasov partition-function relation.** These partition functions satisfy

$$
(-qz^{1/2};q,q)^2_{\infty}\mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{inst}}(i,i,i,iq^{\pm1/2},u;q^{-1},q|z^{1/2})=\mathcal{Z}_{\mathrm{inst}}(u;q^{-1},q^2|z).
$$

The relation is presented as a consequence expected from the tau-function correspondence and was checked computationally through order $z^5$ in the surrounding text; no general proof is supplied.
row.source_name: M. Bershtein and A. Shchechkin, “Painleve equations from Nakajima-Yoshioka blowup relations”, arXiv:1811.04050 (2019).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.04050

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2018).

row.title: Brevier–Preissmann–Sebő strong antipalindromic subsequence conjecture
row.statement:
Let $w$ be a **binary circular word** of length $n$ divisible by $6$ with equal numbers of zeros and ones. A circular word can be represented as a concatenation of linear words, and a subsequence is taken in the corresponding linear representation. An **antipalindrome** is a binary word whose opposite letters are distinct.

**Brevier–Preissmann–Sebő's conjecture.** The word $w$ can be partitioned into two linear words $w_1,w_2$ of equal length, $w=w_1w_2$, having subsequences $s_1,s_2$ such that $s_1s_2$ is an antipalindrome and

$$
|s_1|=|s_2|=\frac{1}{3}|w|.
$$

This strengthens the Lyngsø–Pedersen conjecture by requiring the two halves of the antipalindromic subsequence to come from opposite halves of a balanced cut of the circle. It was checked computationally through $n=30$; the source gives a weaker proved bound with each half of length $\frac14|w|$.
row.source_name: Clemens Müllner and Andrew Ryzhikov, “Palindromic Subsequences in Finite Words”, arXiv:1901.07502 (2019).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1901.07502

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2019).

row.title: Bárány–Larman colorful topological Tverberg conjecture
row.statement:
Let $q \ge 2$ and $d \ge 1$ be integers. Let $C_1, \ldots, C_{d+1}$ be pairwise disjoint sets of vertices of $\Delta_{q(d+1)-1}$, each of size $q$, and let $f\colon \Delta_{q(d+1)-1} \to \mathds{R}^d$ be a continuous map. **Bárány–Larman's colorful topological Tverberg conjecture.** There are $q$ pairwise disjoint faces $\sigma_1, \dots, \sigma_q$ of $\Delta_{q(d+1)-1}$ such that

$$
f(\sigma_1) \cap \dots \cap f(\sigma_q) \ne \emptyset
$$

and each $\sigma_i$ has at most one vertex in each $C_j$. This is a colorful version of the topological Tverberg theorem beyond prime powers; it is known to be open even for affine maps, although it has been verified when $q+1$ is prime.
row.source_name: Florian Frick and Pablo Soberón, “The topological Tverberg problem beyond prime powers”, arXiv:2005.05251 (2023).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.05251

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2020).

row.title: Converse CDE conjecture for shifted Young diagrams
row.statement:
Let $\lambda$ be a shifted Young diagram, and let $[\emptyset,\lambda]$ denote the corresponding lower interval. A shifted Young diagram is **balanced** according to the shifted-diagram notion used in the paper, and it is **trapezoidal** if it has the form $(n,n-2,\dots,n-2k+2)$. The CDE property is the coincidence of the expected down-degree and up-degree statistics with the corresponding rank-uniform averages.

**Converse CDE conjecture for shifted diagrams.** The interval $[\emptyset,\lambda]$ has the CDE property if and only if $\lambda$ is balanced or trapezoidal.

The balanced and trapezoidal sufficient cases are established by results cited in the source. The conjectured converse was verified for shifted Young diagrams of size at most $18$ by Hopkins and up to size $50$ in this paper, but remains open in general.
row.source_name: Jang Soo Kim, Michael J. Schlosser and Meesue Yoo, “Enumeration of standard barely set-valued tableaux of shifted shapes”, arXiv:2006.03253 (2020).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.03253

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2020).

row.title: The London–Paris conjecture for cocircuit paths on topes
row.statement:
Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{M}}$ be a uniform oriented matroid. Let $\operatorname{\mathcal{C}}^*(\operatorname{\mathcal{M}})$ denote its cocircuits, and let $X,Y\in\operatorname{\mathcal{C}}^*(\operatorname{\mathcal{M}})$ be cocircuits that are vertices of at least one tope of $\operatorname{\mathcal{M}}$. For a tope $\operatorname{\mathcal{T}}$, write $d_{\operatorname{\mathcal{T}}}(X,Y)$ for the shortest-path distance between $X$ and $Y$ in the subgraph induced by the vertices of $\operatorname{\mathcal{T}}$.

**London–Paris conjecture.** There exists a tope $\operatorname{\mathcal{T}}$ in $\operatorname{\mathcal{M}}$ such that $X,Y\in\operatorname{\mathcal{T}}$ and

$$
d_{\operatorname{\mathcal{M}}}(X,Y)=d_{\operatorname{\mathcal{T}}}(X,Y).
$$

If true, this would imply a quadratic upper bound on the diameter of polytopes via the improved quadratic bound for cocircuit graphs. The conjecture has been verified computationally for oriented matroids with up to nine elements, but remains open in general.
row.source_name: Ilan Adler, Jesús A. De Loera, Steven Klee and Zhenyang Zhang, “Diameters of Cocircuit Graphs of Oriented Matroids: An Update”, arXiv:2006.08922 (2020).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.08922

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of June 2020). “Then $\diam(G^*(\mathcal{M})) \leq n-r+2.$ Conjecture bears a striking resemblance to the famous Hirsch conjecture for convex polytopes, which was disproved by Santos , and with good reason.”

row.title: The periodic-point avoidance conjecture for consecutive-pattern-avoiding stack-sorting maps
row.statement:
Let $\sigma\in S_k$ with $k\geq 3$. For a permutation, $\operatorname{rev}(\sigma)$ denotes the reversal of $\sigma$, and underlined patterns indicate consecutive-pattern avoidance. The map $\operatorname{SC}_\sigma:S_n\to S_n$ is the consecutive-pattern-avoiding stack-sorting map.

**Periodic-point avoidance conjecture.** The periodic points of $\operatorname{SC}_\sigma$ are precisely the permutations in

$$
\operatorname{Av}_n\left(\underline{\sigma},\underline{\operatorname{rev}(\sigma)}\right).
$$

The claim is confirmed in the paper when $k=4$ and $n\leq 8$; the general assertion remains open.
row.source_name: Colin Defant and Kai Zheng, “Stack-Sorting with Consecutive-Pattern-Avoiding Stacks”, arXiv:2008.12297 (2020).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.12297

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2020).

row.title: The maximal Randić energy conjecture for connected graphs
row.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph, and let $RE(G)$ denote its Randić energy, the sum of the absolute values of the eigenvalues of the Randić matrix of $G$. Among connected graphs of a fixed order, call a graph one with **maximal Randić energy** if its Randić energy is greatest among all connected graphs of that order.

**Maximal Randić energy conjecture.** The connected graph with maximal Randić energy is a tree.

The conjecture was computationally verified for graphs of order $n$ up to $n=10$. A characterization of connected graphs with maximal Randić energy remains open.
row.source_name: Domingos M. Cardoso, Paula Carvalho, Roberto C. Díaz and Paula Rama, “On the Randić energy of caterpillar graphs”, arXiv:2107.11422 (2021).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.11422

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2021). “The following more thinner conjecture, also posed in , remains open too.”

row.title: Complete score conjecture for two-row grids
row.statement:
Let $G_{2,m}$ be the rectangular grid with two rows and $m$ columns, and let $Ls(G_{2,m})$ and $Rs(G_{2,m})$ denote the corresponding left and right scores. **Two-row grid score conjecture.** For $m\geq 2$,

$$
Ls(G_{2,m})=-Rs(G_{2,m})=
\begin{cases}
6 & \text{if } m=3,\\
4 & \text{if } m\equiv 1 \pmod 2 \text{ and } m\geq 5 \text{ or } m=2,\\
2 & \text{if } m\equiv 0 \pmod 2 \text{ and } m\geq 4.
\end{cases}
$$

The preceding theorem and lemma establish part of this pattern, and the source notes that it remains only to prove $Ls(G_{2,m})\leq 2$ for even $m$; the conjecture was checked computationally up to $m=30$.
row.source_name: Eric Duchêne, Nacim Oijid and Aline Parreau, “Bipartite instances of INFLUENCE”, arXiv:2206.06118 (2022).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.06118

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2022).

row.title: Ahanjideh–Akbari–Fakharan–Trevisan conjecture on Laplacian eigenvalues and diameter
row.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph of order $n$, let $d$ be its diameter with $d\ge 2$, and let $m_GI$ denote the number of Laplacian eigenvalues of $G$ in an interval $I\subseteq[0,n]$. The path on $d+1$ vertices is denoted by $P_{d+1}$. **Ahanjideh–Akbari–Fakharan–Trevisan conjecture.** If $G\ne P_{d+1}$, then

$$
m_G[n-d+2,n]\le n-d.
$$

This conjecture concerns the distribution of Laplacian eigenvalues of connected graphs in relation to their diameter. The stated source notes that it was verified when $d\in\{2,3\}$ or when the diameter is at most the independence number; its general status is not specified here.
row.source_name: Leyou Xu and Bo Zhou, “Proof of a conjecture on distribution of Laplacian eigenvalues and diameter, and beyond”, arXiv:2303.11503 (2023).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.11503

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2023).

row.title: Weakly consecutive sequence generation conjecture
row.statement: A **weakly consecutive sequence (WCS)** is a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1,\ldots,k\}$ such that if an integer $d$ divides $\sigma(i)$, then $d$ also divides $\sigma(i\pm d)$ wherever these terms are defined. The paper specifies four starting sequences and three rules for generating WCSs. **Weakly consecutive sequence generation conjecture.** Any WCS can be derived from one of the four starting sequences by applying the three rules. Moreover, for $k\geq 12$, the starting sequence and rule applications are unique up to reordering the rules. This has been verified computationally up to $k=500$, while uniqueness is false for $k\leq 11$; the asserted sufficiency of the starting sequences and rules remains unproved.
row.source_name: Thomas Garrison, Chris Seiler and Andrew Knowles, “Weakly Consecutive Sequences”, arXiv:2401.09497 (2024).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.09497

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2024).

row.title: Real-rootedness and root-location conjecture for generalized snake posets
row.statement:
Let $\mathbf{w}$ be a generalized snake word of length $n+1$. Let $h^*(\mathbf{w};z)$ denote its $h^*$-polynomial, and let $L(\mathcal{O}(P(\mathbf{w}));t)$ denote the Ehrhart polynomial of the order polytope $\mathcal{O}(P(\mathbf{w}))$. **Conjecture for generalized snake words.** All roots of $h^*(\mathbf{w};z)$ are real and negative, and all roots of $L(\mathcal{O}(P(\mathbf{w}));t)$ are contained in the disk

$$
\left|z-\frac{n+4}{2}\right|\leq\frac{n+2}{2},\qquad z\in\mathbb{C},
$$

with axis of symmetry $x=\frac{-n-4}{2}$. The conjecture was verified for snake words of length up to $9$, but the general assertions remain open.
row.source_name: Eon Lee, Andrés R. Vindas-Meléndez and Zhi Wang, “Generalized snake posets, order polytopes, and lattice-point enumeration”, arXiv:2411.18695 (2026).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.18695

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2024).

row.title: Unique NAC-colouring conjecture for minimally rigid graphs
row.statement:
Let $G$ be a minimally rigid graph. **Unique NAC-colouring conjecture.** We have

$$
\operatorname{NAC}_{\#}(G)=1
$$

if and only if either $G\in\mathcal{G}_{sc}$ and it has exactly one $3$-prism subgraph, or $G$ is a $0$-extension graph with exactly one open step. The conjecture has been verified by computer for graphs on up to $10$ vertices; the stated graph families are known to satisfy $\operatorname{NAC}_{\#}(G)=1$, but the converse remains open.
row.source_name: Katie Clinch, Dániel Garamvölgyi, John Haslegrave, Tony Huynh, Jan Legerský and Anthony Nixon, “Stable cuts, NAC-colourings and flexible realisations of graphs”, arXiv:2412.16018 (2026).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.16018

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2024).

row.title: Vertex-localized Elphick–Linz–Wocjan conjecture
row.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with vertex set $V$. For each vertex $v$, let $c(v)$ denote the relevant local clique parameter, and let $s^+(G)$ denote the sum of the squares of the positive eigenvalues of the adjacency matrix of $G$. **Vertex-localized Elphick–Linz–Wocjan conjecture.** For any graph $G$,

$$
\sqrt{s^+(G)}\leq \sum_{v\in V}\left(1-\frac{1}{c(v)}\right).
$$

The conjecture is proved for diamond-free graphs and almost all Erdős–Rényi random graphs $G(n,1/2)$, and was computationally verified for graphs up to $9$ vertices; the general case remains open.
row.source_name: M. Rajesh Kannan, Hitesh Kumar and Shivaramakrishna Pragada, “Localization of spectral Turán-type theorems”, arXiv:2512.01409 (2025).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.01409

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).

row.title: Wang–Xia's conjecture on the first Steklov eigenvalue
row.statement:
Let $(M^n,g)$, with $ngeq 2$, be a connected compact smooth Riemannian manifold with boundary. Assume that $\operatorname{Ric}_g\geq 0$ and that the principal curvatures of the boundary $\partial M$ are bounded below by a constant $c>0$. Denote by $\lambda_1=\lambda_1(\partial M)$ the first nonzero eigenvalue of the Laplacian of $\partial M$. Let $\xi_1$ be the first nonzero Steklov eigenvalue.

**Wang–Xia's conjecture.** The eigenvalue $\xi_1$ satisfies

$$
\xi_1\geq \frac{n+2}{n-1}c\lambda_1,
$$

with equality only for the Euclidean ball of radius $1/c$.

This conjecture was stated by Qiaoling Wang and Changyu Xia and is verified in the paper for warped product manifolds when $n=3$ and $m=1$. Its status in the generality stated above is not resolved by the supplied source.
row.source_name: Zongyi Lv, Changwei Xiong and Yuxun Zou, “Scaling inequalities for Steklov eigenvalues in space forms and sharp eigenvalue estimates on warped product manifolds”, arXiv:2512.22885 (2025).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.22885

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2025).

row.title: Kalai's cascade consequence for higher Tverberg partitions
row.statement:
Let $d,r$ be positive integers and let $k$ be a non-negative integer. A **Tverberg $(r+1)$-partition** of a finite point set is a partition into $r+1$ parts whose convex hulls have a common point. **Kalai's cascade consequence.** If $S$ is a set of $(r-1)(d+1)+k+2$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ and

$$
\dim(T_r(S))\leq k,
$$

then $S$ has at least one Tverberg $(r+1)$-partition. This is presented as a direct consequence of Kalai's cascade conjecture and remains unconfirmed except when $r=1$ or $d\leq 2$; the case $r=1$ is Radon's theorem.
row.source_name: Pablo Soberón, “Tverberg cores and Kalai's cascade conjecture”, arXiv:2605.21305 (2026).
row.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2021–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2103.08421](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.08421).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.21305

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2026). “remains open even for small values of \(r\) and \(d\).”

row.title: Burr–Erdős–Faudree–Rousseau–Schelp conjecture for star forests
row.statement:
Let $s$ and $t$ be positive integers. Let $n_{1}\geq n_{2}\geq \cdots\geq n_{s}\geq 1$ and $m_{1}\geq m_{2}\geq \cdots\geq m_{t}\geq 1$ be integers, and for each $k\in [s+t]\backslash [1]$ define

$$
\ell_{k}=\max\left\{n_{i}+m_{j}-1:i+j=k\right\}.
$$

**Burr–Erdős–Faudree–Rousseau–Schelp conjecture.** The size Ramsey number of the two star forests satisfies

$$
\hat{r}\left(\bigsqcup_{i=1}^{s}K_{1,n_{i}},\bigsqcup_{j=1}^{t}K_{1,m_{j}}\right)=\sum_{k=2}^{s+t}\ell_{k}.
$$

This conjecture was confirmed for uniform star forests and for several further cases, including when all $n_i$ and $m_j$ are odd or when $s=1$, but it remains open in general.
row.source_name: Pingting Fu, Zhidan Luo and Zhenyu Ni, “Size Ramsey minimal graphs for uniform star forests”, arXiv:2606.04439 (2026).
row.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2021–2026). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2506.10477](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.10477), [arXiv:2111.02065](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.02065).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04439

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2026).

row.title: Polynomial product formula conjecture for the generalized Aztec-diamond matrix
row.statement:
Let $A(k,t)$ be the skew-symmetric matrix whose entries satisfy

$$
\begin{cases}
a_{1,j}=t, & j>1,\\
a_{i,j}=a_{i-1,j}+a_{i,j-1}+a_{i-1,j-1}, & j>i+1,\quad i>1,\\
a_{i,j}=a_{i-1,j}+a_{i-1,j-1}+k(-1)^{i-1}, & j=i+1,\quad i>1,\\
a_{i,j}=-a_{j,i}, & j\leq i.
\end{cases}
$$

Write $A_{[2n]}(k,t)$ for its leading $2n\times 2n$ principal submatrix, and let $\mathsf{pf}$ denote the Pfaffian.

**Generalized product formula conjecture.** There exists a sequence of polynomials $o_n(k,t)\in\mathbb{Z}[k,t]$ such that

$$
\mathsf{pf}(A_{[2n]}(k,t))=t\,o_{n-1}(k,t)o_n(k,t).
$$

The conjecture has been checked by computer up to $n=25$. Setting $k=t=2$ recovers the preceding product formula conjecture, while a proof for general $k$ and $t$ remains open.
row.source_name: Yi-Lin Lee, “Off-diagonally symmetric domino tilings of the Aztec diamond”, arXiv:2303.02750 (2023).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.02750

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2023).

row.title: The orbit-representation conjecture for integral points of $X_{N,y}$
row.statement:
Let $N\in\mathbb{N}$ and $y\in\Gamma_N$. Let $\eta\in X_{N,y}(\mathbb{Z})$ be an integral point. For $\widehat{w}\in\Sigma W^0$ and $g\in G$, define the action $g\cdot\widehat{w}$ as in the preceding notation. **Orbit-representation conjecture.** There exist $\widehat{w}\in\Sigma W^0$ and $g\in G$ such that

$$
g\cdot\widehat{w}=\eta.
$$

This conjecture is presented as a natural analogue of the earlier result referred to as the conjecture in the source, and has been checked for the first values of $N$ up to $N=1000$. Its general validity remains open.
row.source_name: Olivier Brunat, Nathan Chapelier-Laget and Thomas Gerber, “Generalised core partitions and Diophantine equations”, arXiv:2403.11191 (2025).
row.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.11191

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2024).
